stories.title: Trump says US is officially renaming AI ‘super intelligence’
stories.simple_summary: Donald Trump said during a speech that the US is officially changing the name of 'artificial intelligence' to 'super intelligence' because he thinks the word 'artificial' makes it sound fake.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just a name change by the government — it won't affect how AI actually works or how you use it.

stories.title: Trump and Xi to Discuss A.I. Risks and Competition at US-China Summit
stories.simple_summary: The US and China are planning to talk about AI safety risks and competition between their countries.
stories.why_it_matters: When big countries negotiate about technology, it can eventually affect what AI tools are available and how they're regulated, but this is just a discussion being planned.

stories.title: Three out of four Americans say AI firms not doing enough to prevent disaster, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
stories.simple_summary: A poll found that three out of four Americans think AI companies aren't doing enough to protect people from potential dangers.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows many people are worried about AI safety, which might push companies to be more careful — but it doesn't mean disaster is coming.

stories.title: The world freaked out about AI doomsday. Now what?
stories.simple_summary: People have been worried about AI causing big problems, but now the headlines are calming down and the article asks what comes next.
stories.why_it_matters: The panic around AI isn't matching reality, which is normal — fear often goes up and down, then life continues as usual.

stories.title: Everyone can find a reason to dislike data center construction
stories.simple_summary: Building large data centers (the computer warehouses that run AI) in Pennsylvania has caused a lot of local disagreement over two years.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people in Pennsylvania — it shows communities are concerned about where AI infrastructure gets built.

stories.title: Nscale’s IPO will test Wall Street’s appetite for concentrated AI bets once again
stories.simple_summary: A British company that builds AI data centers is planning to sell stock to the public, and its success depends heavily on Microsoft and another company buying from it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to investors — nothing you need to pay attention to unless you're buying stocks.

stories.title: Meta patches Muse exploit that let attackers control the AI agent
stories.simple_summary: Meta found and fixed a security weakness in its Muse AI tool that could have let hackers take control of it.
stories.why_it_matters: This was already fixed, so there's no danger to you — it just shows that companies need to keep watching for security problems.

stories.title: New York tightens AI regulations as technology rapidly evolves
stories.simple_summary: New York state is making stronger rules about how AI companies can operate.
stories.why_it_matters: More regulations might make AI safer for everyone, but the details matter and we'd need to see what the rules actually are.

stories.title: Not Micron. Not Alphabet. Here's My Top Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Pick for the Next 3 Years.
stories.simple_summary: An investment newsletter is recommending a particular AI-related stock for people to buy.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investment advice — nothing you need to act on unless you're actively buying stocks and want that company's opinion.

stories.title: 5 Ways AI Is Reshaping Student Success
stories.simple_summary: Schools and colleges are using AI in five different ways to help students learn better.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids or grandkids in school, AI might be helping them study, but you don't need to do anything about it.

stories.title: Alex Berenson: I Didn’t Fall for Covid Fearmongering. But AI Terrifies Me.
stories.simple_summary: A writer says he's worried about AI in a way he wasn't worried about COVID.
stories.why_it_matters: This is one person's opinion about AI risks — it doesn't mean AI is actually dangerous right now.

stories.title: The man who built Apple’s stores doesn’t buy Silicon Valley’s bet on AI shopping
stories.simple_summary: The person who designed Apple's physical stores says Apple shouldn't count on AI to replace the people who help customers shop in stores.
stories.why_it_matters: Some business experts think AI shopping won't replace humans the way some people claim, but this doesn't change how you shop now.
